findings.text: Exposes a whole folio removal helper that validates the folio still belongs to the supplied cache, then detaches mappings, releases filesystem state, clears dirtiness and drops the cache reference. Mismatch is reported as an input output failure rather than proceeding.

Exposes a byte range truncation service over a cache. It normalizes inclusive byte bounds into page indices, discards fully covered entries in batches, processes edge folios that straddle boundaries, then reaps leftovers until the interval is empty. An all ones lend denotes file end.

Provides two shmem range discard entry shapes observed in fragments: one delegates to a shmem specific undo walk and refreshes modification, change and version metadata, the other delegates directly to the generic page cache range discard. Both accept start inclusive and end inclusive bounds.

Exposes a swap type reclamation scan that walks the global swapped inode registry and pages swapped entries of the requested type back into their caches, pruning entries that no longer hold swapped pages and yielding the processor between inodes.

Exposes writeback hooks that attempt to move a folio to swap instead of filesystem storage. The vector form takes a submit context plus an optional split overflow list, the single form builds a local context and submits immediately. Both return an activate directive with the folio still locked when swap cannot be used.

Defines final teardown for shmem inodes: unaccount charge, clear size, mark cache exiting, discard entire range, detach from shrink and swap registries with waiting for concurrent reclamation, release extended attributes, free inode charge, warn on leftover blocks and drop quota state.

Defines attribute query and mutation for shmem. Query reconciles allocation accounting when cached counts drift, mirrors append immutable and nodump flags into statx, fills generic attributes, widens block size under huge mode and supplies birth time. Mutation enforces seals and frozen state, adjusts size accounting and discards shrunken tails with surrounding unmaps.

A folio is only discarded from a cache when its current owner matches the target cache. The shmem undo path treats a mismatch as replacement by a swap entry and retries the slot, while the generic whole folio helper fails the operation.

Cleanup detaches process mappings first, then asks the filesystem to release folio private state over the full extent, and only afterwards cancels dirtiness, because some filesystems may dirty again during release. Partial cleanup zeroes visible bytes unless the cache is inaccessible, then releases the subrange.
Invalidation is optional and delegated to the owning cache operations vector when present. Absence of a handler means no action is required.

Partial truncation reports whether the caller must adjust its whole folio sweep bounds. Success means the range was zeroed, split or dropped; a negative style outcome means the folio stayed dirty after an unsuccessful split and the caller narrows start or end around it.

Large folio handling attempts division toward the cache minimum order at page aligned boundaries for the range start and, when useful, the range end. A trailing end aligned exactly to folio end skips the second division attempt.

Size and permission mutations are refused when seals forbid them: execution seal blocks execute bit flips, shrink and grow seals block respective size moves, and a frozen mapping flag blocks any size change. Quota and access control updates still proceed only after these checks.

Swapout divides a large folio when it straddles the allocation horizon derived from size or when multi size swap is unavailable. Division preserves dirtiness beforehand and clears it on the divided head while accounting a fallback event per order.

Folios are locked while validating ownership, waiting for writeback, zeroing, invalidating, splitting or removing from cache, and unlocked before batch release or retry. Second half acquisition during dual split uses non blocking lock with reference pinning and revalidation.

Removal of non folio cache values takes the host inode lock plus the cache index write lock with workingset node accounting, then optionally rejoins the inode to the reclaim list when the cache is shrinkable. Shmem caches bypass this path entirely.

The global swapped inode list and per inode swap membership are mutated under a dedicated swap list lock. Scanners raise a per inode stop counter before dropping the lock so eviction waits instead of detaching or freeing the inode, and wake waiters when the counter reaches zero.

Shrink membership changes are serialized by a filesystem wide shrink lock with an empty check repeated inside. In progress fallocation ranges tracked through inode private data are inspected under the inode lock and only credited when the folio index lies inside the unfinished window.

Range discard proceeds in three sweeps: bulk removal of fully interior folios, single locked handling of start and end straddlers with possible bound tightening, and a final reaping loop that restarts from the beginning unless forward progress proves completion.

Shmem undo iterates over locked batch entries, skipping holes that are not up to date only under punch semantics, retrying slots whose owner changed, splitting or discarding large folios, resetting the scan to the beginning after a successful division, and finally adjusting swapped accounting.

Per inode swap recovery repeatedly collects a batch of matching swap values starting from the last processed index, swaps each back into cache, and continues until a collection round finds nothing or reports a fatal error. Out of memory aborts the current inode but preserves earlier progress.

Swapout moves from eligibility checks to optional splitting, then to folio initialization, swap allocation with accounting and registry insertion, cache replacement by a swap value, submission, and on reactivation reinstatement with accounting rollback and swap cache detachment; any ineligible or failed step falls through to dirty and activate.

Concurrent fault, copy on write and swap replacement can repopulate mappings during truncation. The code defends by unmapping both before and after shrinking, by retrying when ownership changes, by revalidating pinned second halves, and by tolerating swap erasure when reinserting after reactivation.

Failed division normally forces an unmap so later faults observe size boundaries, with an assertion that no mapping remains, except for shmem caches which historically retain huge mappings beyond size and therefore skip the forced unmap.

Eviction warns when block accounting remains after full discard, indicating leaked reservation. Exceptional cleanup warns when direct access entries survive into truncation, deletes them to avoid an unbounded loop, and assumes filesystems already broke layouts under lock.

Truncation paths wait for writeback before modifying contents and assert that writeback is absent at discard time in the shmem undo walk, reflecting an invariant that locked folios selected for discard are not under writeback.
An end bound of all ones bits denotes truncation through file end and expands to the maximum page index. Callers pass minus one cast to the unsigned end type for this purpose.

Shmem exposes append, immutable and nodump filesystem flags through statx attribute bits and mask, reports huge block size when huge mode is globally enabled, and always supplies birth time from its creation timestamp.

Observed shmem inode state includes allocated and swapped page counts, filesystem flags, seals, frozen flag, shrink and swap list nodes, stop counter, fallocation tracking pointer, creation time and extended attribute storage; cache state includes page count and exiting flag used during teardown.

Policy display emits a formatted policy string only when a non default policy object is present, with a build variant that does nothing. Synchronous wake delegates to the default wake action then detaches the waiter so it triggers once.
